newsitem.title: GERMANY: German July inflation highest since June '95.
newsitem.headline: German July inflation highest since June '95.

text.p: German inflation rose to 1.9 percent year-on-year in July, its highest rate since June 1995, the Federal Statistics Office said Tuesday.
The month-on-month rise in the consumer price index was 0.5 percent, the highest since January 1997. In June, the increases were 1.7 percent year-on-year and 0.2 percent from the previous month.
The figures back up a warning made last week by Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing that German prices were moving "in the wrong direction."
Issing's remarks may have been a hint that the central bank could begin to nudge interest rates higher to combat inflation and the weak mark.

In west Germany, the year-on-year increase in consumer prices in July was 1.7 percent, and 0.4 percent month-on-month. This was lower than preliminary data released last month showing rises of 1.8 percent and 0.5 percent respectively.
In the former communist east Germany, consumer prices rose 2.4 percent from the year-earlier month, and 0.7 percent from June.

The Statistics Office said one of the main reasons for the relatively strong increase in prices was a rise in the share of the cost of medicines that consumers must pay. Without that increase, consumer prices would have been only 0.3 percent higher than in June, it said.
